statement: When a personal data breach is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller must communicate the breach to the data subject without undue delay, describing in clear and plain language the nature of the breach and containing at least the information and measures referred to in points (b), (c) and (d) of Article 33(3) (GDPR Article 34(1)-(2)).
caveat: Communication is not required where the affected data were protected by measures such as encryption, where subsequent measures ensure the high risk is no longer likely to materialise, or where it would involve disproportionate effort, in which case a public communication or similar measure informs data subjects in an equally effective manner (Art. 34(3)(a)-(c)); a supervisory authority may also require communication or rule that an exception is met (Art. 34(4)). Verified against the Official Journal text on the Publications Office cellar (eur-lex.europa.eu was unreachable to automated fetches at check time). This repo does not assess breach risk.
